C1.statement: Superconducting: τ*_log < τ*_phys (empirical), with the learned decoder, in both bases. Trapped ion with crosstalk off: no idle-driven optimum. Trapped ion with crosstalk at the card value: an interior τ*_log < τ*_phys appears
C1.note: Provisional (A50). Superconducting refuted against tau*_phys (empirical); not held: Z d5 soft refuted [0.586, 0.957] us; X d5 hard refuted [0.658, 0.944] us; X d5 soft refuted [0.729, 1.05] us. Ion, pre-registered point flag: off refuted (Z d3 hard, Z d3 soft), card rate undetermined (2 of 6 rows flagged), any rate held. Resolved flag (DECISIONS E12, added after seeing the data): off held, card rate refuted, any rate held. Rows with fractionTied >= 0.5 are UNRESOLVED and excluded.

C2.statement: Soft decoding is at or below hard at every τ, with most gain where readouts are short
C2.note: Provisional (A50). Soft above hard beyond the Wilson intervals: Z trapped-ion 0 of 39; Z superconducting 0 of 36; X trapped-ion 0 of 39; X superconducting 0 of 36. Wilson intervals treat the R readout draws of a shot as independent; cluster and paired intervals come at CC-A19 and the counts are redone at A53a.

C3.statement: Neither readout model dominates: along the τ grids the ion arm has lower error per round and the superconducting arm more rounds per second
C3.note: Provisional (A50). At tau*_log (d = 3, hard, learned): ion 0.00112 [0.000928, 0.00135] per round at 253 rounds/s; superconducting 0.00217 [0.00189, 0.00248] at 9.11e+5 rounds/s; neither dominates. With these cards the outcome is fixed by construction (cycle times differ by orders of magnitude and the gate noise is shared); reported with informative: false at A53c (DECISIONS E12).

C4.statement: Break-even ε̄ (d = 5 beats d = 3) similar on both arms, on the empirical ε̄ axis
C4.note: Provisional (A50). Empirical axis, learned: hard: ion 0.237, superconducting — (|diff| — against sum of half-widths —) undetermined; soft: ion —, superconducting — (|diff| — against sum of half-widths —) undetermined.

C5.statement: The learned detector error model lowers the logical error against the naive one at every (d, arm, mode) at τ*_log, out of sample
C5.note: Provisional (A50), IN SAMPLE: the learned rates come from the banks being decoded, so this does not test "out of sample"; V12(b) failed (DECISIONS E4) and the held-out test V18 decides it at A53b. Learned above naive beyond the Wilson intervals at 0 of 24 points; below beyond them at 19.

C6.statement: In the phase-flip memory the superconducting τ*_log is shorter than in the bit-flip memory when T2 < T1
C6.note: Not applicable with the card: the statement is conditional on T2 < T1, and the card has T2 = 77 us >= T1 = 50 us (DECISIONS E7, E12). The rule on these files gives "undetermined"; C6 is tested with a variant card (T2 = 25 us, UNSOURCED, illustrative) at CC-A19.

O4.statement: Ratio of bulk detector rates, X-basis to Z-basis banks, per (d, r): how biased forte-1 noise looks to the decoder (measurement, no hypothesis)
O4.note: Measurement, no hypothesis (no verdict). X over Z bulk detector rate (dem_forte1.json -> ratioXoverZ): d3 r1 1.041 [0.894, 1.213]; d3 r3 1.027 [0.959, 1.100]; d5 r3 1.000 [0.953, 1.048]; d5 r5 1.029 [0.995, 1.064]; d7 r3 1.021 [0.983, 1.061]; 5 of 5 intervals contain 1 (DECISIONS E5).

two_qubit_gate_us.source: IonQ Forte 1, 2-q gate speed 970 us (ZZ gate) at job submission: Robertson et al., 'Variational Gibbs State Preparation on Trapped-Ion Devices', arXiv:2603.03801 (2026), Table 1. For comparison: Aria two-qubit gate 600 us (Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider page, Aria system timing); Forte Enterprise 1 650 us (same Table 1)

gate_layers_per_round.source: conservative choice: the 2(d-1) CNOTs of a round run one after another on the single chain (no published statement found that IonQ Forte runs two-qubit gates on disjoint pairs in parallel; simultaneous entangling gates in one chain are demonstrated only in research systems). See DECISIONS E8

reset_us.source: IonQ Forte 1, reset speed 50 us at job submission: Robertson et al., arXiv:2603.03801 (2026), Table 1 (Aria 1: 20 us; Forte Enterprise 1: 150 us, same table)

two_qubit_gate_us.source: Google Quantum AI, 'Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold', Nature 638, 920 (2025), arXiv:2408.13687, Supplementary Information Section I: CZ gates in 42 ns on the 105-qubit processor (37 ns on the 72-qubit processor)

gate_layers_per_round.source: derived: each round is two parallel CNOT layers

reset_us.source: multi-level reset to the ground state, total duration about 250 ns (error about 1e-3): McEwen et al., 'Removing leakage-induced correlated errors in superconducting quantum error correction', Nat. Commun. 12, 1761 (2021), arXiv:2102.06131, main text (Fig. 2 discussion: 'The total duration of the reset protocol is about 250 ns'; checked against the arXiv PDF Sat 10 Oct). Google's 1.1 us surface-code cycle (arXiv:2408.13687) gives no reset duration

R_bright_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), 171Yb+ with SNSPD, Results (Fig. 2a discussion): overall photon detection rate 472(14) kcps = 0.472 counts/us (collected, system efficiency 4.356%)

R_dark_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results and Methods: background count rate 4.2(1) cps = 4.2e-6 counts/us

gamma_bright_to_dark_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results (Fig. 2a discussion): dark pumping rate 341(13) Hz = 3.41e-4 /us

gamma_dark_to_bright_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results (Fig. 2a discussion): bright pumping rate 16.4(5) Hz = 1.64e-5 /us

T1_idle_us.source: Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider documentation (learn.microsoft.com/azure/quantum/provider-ionq), IonQ Aria, System timing: T1 10-100 s (same 171Yb+ qubit as Forte; no Forte T1 is published there); lower end 10 s = 1e7 us used (conservative)

T2_idle_us.source: Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider documentation (learn.microsoft.com/azure/quantum/provider-ionq), IonQ Aria, System timing: T2 1 s (same 171Yb+ qubit as Forte; no Forte T2 is published there) = 1e6 us; satisfies T2 <= 2 T1

crosstalk_rate_per_us.source: Gaebler et al., arXiv:2108.10932 (2021), Honeywell H0, 171Yb+, Table 2: probe-qubit average error with an interleaved dark measurement of a qubit 110 um away, minus the control: 1.3e-3 - 0.31e-3 = 1.0e-3 per 120 us detection (zone 2, micromotion hiding at 2.3 um on); converted with 1/2 (1 - exp(-Gamma tau)) = 1.0e-3 at tau = 120 us: Gamma = -ln(1 - 2e-3) / 120 us = 1.67e-5 /us. Lower bound for a same-species chain: unshielded and a few um apart, neighbours see more (the scan covers up to 1e-3 /us)

crosstalk_scan_per_us.source: scan grid spanning shielded to unshielded same-species chains; illustrative

tau_grid_us.source: spans the published detection-time range: 10.5-181.6 us (Noek et al., Opt. Lett. 38, 4735 (2013)), 11 us average and 500 us fixed window (Crain et al. 2019); 1-7 us added to resolve the short-time, photon-starved regime

chi_over_2pi_MHz.source: representative transmon value (plan section 7.4 default), not one device; published dispersive shifts span ~0.5-8 MHz, e.g. |chi|/2pi = 7.9 MHz in Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017), arXiv:1701.06933

kappa_over_2pi_MHz.source: chosen as kappa = 2 chi, the optimum of kappa |delta alpha|^2 at fixed nbar (plan section 7); Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017) use the same design rule with a Purcell filter, kappa_eff/2pi = 37.5 MHz

nbar.source: UNSOURCED (illustrative): a few photons, below typical critical photon numbers; plan section 7.4 default

eta.source: representative heterodyne chain with a quantum-limited amplifier (plan section 7.4 default); Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017) report eta = 0.66 with a phase-sensitive parametric amplifier, so 0.3 is conservative

T1_us.source: representative transmon T1 (plan section 7.4 default), within the published range from 7.6 us (Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017)) to a few hundred us in current devices

T2_us.source: Norris et al., arXiv:2503.12603 (2025), Sec. 3, device A qubit 2: median T1 = 50 us (matches T1_us) and median Hahn-echo T2 = 77 us over 104 measurements (Ramsey T2* = 50 us); echo value used for an idle with refocusing; satisfies T2 <= 2 T1 = 100 us

tau_grid_us.source: spans published integration times: 48-88 ns (Walter et al. 2017) up to the few-us regime where T1 decay dominates

definitions.cycleTime: layers * two_qubit_gate_us + tau + reset_us; layers = gate_layers_per_round (a number, or "2*(d-1)" evaluated at d: sequential ion gates, DECISIONS E8)
definitions.tradeoff: per d and mode, at every grid tau: roundsPerSecond and perRound = 0.5 (1 - (1 - 2 pL)^(1/r)); lo and hi are perRound of the Wilson bounds
definitions.perRound: 0.5 (1 - (1 - 2 pL)^(1/r)) at tau*_log; pL and its Wilson bounds interpolated linearly in ln tau between grid points (the best grid point when tau*_log is at the grid edge)
definitions.perMicrosecond: perRound / cycleTime at tau*_log and d
definitions.budgetAtOptimum: Stage 2/3 budget arrays interpolated in ln tau at tau*_log (d = 3, hard, learned); gate is the mean of the learned edge classes
definitions.breakEven: first sign change of pL(d=5) - pL(d=3) in tau order, x axis averageAssignmentError() (belief; empiricalAxis: the F1 empirical curve); interval from the crossings of hi5 - lo3 and lo5 - hi3 (Wilson) on the same grid segment
definitions.conclusions: C1-C6 and O4 follow team checklist Section 1.2 (statements verbatim) with the rules in tools/sweep.mjs (c1Conclusion ... o4Conclusion); verdict equals automated until Person A reviews it; plain is filled at A55
definitions.tieRule: a tau*_log with fractionTied >= 0.5 is UNRESOLVED and excluded from verdicts (DECISIONS E12)
definitions.sensitivityVerdicts: C1-C4 in sensitivity rows keep the v1 rules (holds / flips / undetermined) on the reduced runs; effect is the per-round error and tau*_log at d = 3, hard, learned, at the same reduced statistics (compare with sensitivityBaseline.effect). T2 parameters do not enter the Z-basis (bit-flip) memory, so their rows equal the baseline
definitions.C1v1: superconducting: interior tau*_log below tau*_phys (empirical); trapped-ion: idle flip probability below 0.000001 at every tau, or no interior tau*_log

provenance.seedRule: reduced decode seed = 4000000 + (superconducting ? 100000 : 0) + 10000*d + 1000*logical + tauIndex (same in every rerun; hard and soft share it); shot subsample seed 401 + 10*d + logical; F1 seed 402
